endorsements.quote: Standardized Documentation: In alignment with recent Joint Commission guidance, which underscores the necessity of institutional accountability for AI performance in local clinical contexts, the outcomes of these deliberations should be recorded in an institution-authored Model Card23, distinct from the developer’s.

A VTR committee should be integrated into procurement and implementation governance and include frontline clinicians, operational leaders, quality and safety officers, risk management, compliance, and clinical ethicists representing patient interests26.

These Model Cards should be disseminated internally to frontline users and, where feasible, anonymized and shared across institutions to begin building a national evidence base of collective clinical experience.

unlisted_practices: Require developers to disclose configurable parameters and their associated clinical trade-offs through standardized Model Cards during FDA pre-market review.
Conduct a standardized Value-Tradeoff Review before deploying each AI system that explicitly weighs competing priorities such as sensitivity versus specificity.
Document in an institution-authored Model Card the optimized performance metric, the rationale for adjusting or accepting default settings, and the patient populations most affected.
Link CMS reimbursement or quality incentives to submission of institution-specific Model Cards documenting local calibration choices.
Promote ONC interoperability standards that support local AI parameter adjustment within electronic health records.
Develop accreditation and certification criteria for safe and transparent AI implementation.
Share anonymized institutional Model Cards across institutions to build a national evidence base.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper proposing governance practices (standardized Model Cards and multidisciplinary institutional review) to safeguard clinical value judgment in AI deployment.
